title: OpenAI Internal Model Proves the Euclidean Plane Is Not Five-Colorable (χ(ℝ²) ≥ 6) in Lean 4
aiSystem: OpenAI Internal Frontier Math Model + Lean 4
whyItMatters: Pushes the chromatic number of the Euclidean plane from ≥ 5 (de Grey, 2018) to ≥ 6—narrowing the 1950 Hadwiger–Nelson problem to {6, 7} with an independently kernel-replayed 70-module Lean 4 proof.
summary: As a centerpiece of OpenAI’s mathematical formalization suite (family 158, Erdős Problem #508), an unreleased internal OpenAI model constructed and formally verified in Lean 4 + Comparator a proof that the unit-distance graph of the Euclidean plane cannot be 5-colored, raising the lower bound on the chromatic number of the plane to χ(ℝ²) ≥ 6 for the first time since Aubrey de Grey’s 2018 breakthrough (≥ 5). Independent verification by Erdős Problem a Day replayed all 70 Lean 4 modules from scratch using standard axioms only and audited the proof with seven hostile referee checks, finding zero logical gaps.
technicalHighlights: Advances the 1950 Hadwiger–Nelson problem (Erdős #508) for the first time since 2018, narrowing χ(ℝ²) to either 6 or 7.
Formalized across 70 Lean 4 modules verified with Comparator and standard axioms only.
Independently kernel-replayed and audited with zero gaps by Erdős Problem a Day’s multi-referee review.
caveats: Part of OpenAI’s non-peer-reviewed bulk math repository, though unlike unrefereed manuscripts in the dump, family 158 has been independently kernel-replayed and line-audited.

scoreRationale.foundational: Resolves a landmark step on one of the most famous open problems in discrete geometry (1950), narrowing χ(ℝ²) to just two possibilities.
scoreRationale.ripple: Directly supplied rigidity lemmas reused by Plasma AI to prove Erdős #173 and catalyzed community formal-audit workflows.
scoreRationale.verification: 70-module Lean 4 + Comparator proof independently kernel-replayed and audited with zero gaps.
scoreRationale.velocity: Surpassed decades of SAT-assisted human searches for 6-chromatic unit-distance graphs.
